Environmental analytics


RafikiArdhi turns field data, remote sensing and terrain into maps, models and uncertainty estimates that land managers, researchers and development programmes can act on.

title: Evidence for decisions about land, soil and water
text:
What we do


Soil and landscape mapping
Depth-consistent digital soil maps, soil property surfaces and functional domains, from plot to national scale. 


Hydrology and runoff
Hydrologic soil groups, curve numbers and runoff parameters, and soil-water flux modelling across hillslopes.  


Geostatistics and uncertainty
Variograms, kriging, mixed models and uncertainty propagation, so every map comes with an honest error estimate. 


Decision support
Turning model output and its uncertainty into clear, policy-ready classes and priorities.

title: Evidence for decisions about land, soil and water
text:
How we work
RafikiArdhi takes on environmental problems where existing methods fall short. We develop a method suited to the problem, validate it against real data, and, where agreements allow, release it as an open tool so the knowledge keeps building rather than resetting with each project.
Clients get the solution, and the expertise to apply it to their own data and decisions.

title: Evidence for decisions about land, soil and water
text:
Example: making GIS depth-aware
GIS platforms treat soil as a stack of flat layers, so properties jump at every layer boundary and anything between the standard depths is lost. We built a physics-informed depth spline that runs inside Google Earth Engine, turning a spatially explicit platform into one that is also depth-aware. Each pixel carries a continuous, physically consistent profile, so properties can be read at any depth or integrated over the whole profile, and new layers such as moisture or temperature can be added to the same framework.



Soil organic carbon from the depth spline: maps at six standard depths (left) and the whole-profile total from integrating each pixel’s continuous profile (right).

title: Tools
text: RafikiArdhi builds methods for problems where standard tools fall short, and releases them where agreements allow. The free tools below handle common tasks. The advanced versions use continuous, physics-consistent functions and are available through a project or licence.

title: Tools
text:
Free tools


phySpline: profile harmonisation
Converts soil profiles sampled at any depths to standard depth intervals (for example GlobalSoilMap 0–5, 5–15, 15–30 cm) with a physics-informed spline, so profiles from different surveys can be compared and mapped together. Classes are estimated along a continuous ordered gradient, so the harmoniser can identify transitional classes that were not described in the original horizons.
rafikisol on GitHub →


Carbon stocks
Soil organic carbon stocks for many profiles at once, from carbon concentration, bulk density, coarse fragments and layer thickness, summed over the depth you choose.
Online version coming soon.

title: Tools
text:
Advanced tools
These are RafikiArdhi’s in-house tools, applied in projects or licensed on request. Contact us to discuss your data.


holoSpline
Depth functions that harmonise continuous properties and ordered classes, with an uncertainty estimate at every depth. Profiles can be evaluated at any depth, not only at standard intervals.


Integrated carbon stocks
Stocks integrated over each continuous profile rather than summed layer by layer. Discrete summation can substantially overestimate stocks; integration removes that bias.


Depth-aware mapping in Google Earth Engine
The physics-informed spline running pixel by pixel in Earth Engine, so maps carry a continuous profile and can be read at any depth or integrated over the whole profile.


2D soil-water flux across hillslopes
Steady-state, variably saturated flow across a catena of soil patches, fitted to sensor data. Returns head, water content and fluxes anywhere on the transect, with checks against continuity and Darcy’s law.


Sensor-to-head preparation
Calibrates water-retention parameters per layer, converts sensor water content to pressure and total head, and estimates how much head error is simply sensor noise.


Analytical map updating
Updates an existing soil map with newer data through a closed-form, process-constrained model, and reports how much information each update adds, so knowledge accumulates rather than being replaced.

title: About
text:
Founder and principal scientist
Trevan Flynn holds a PhD in soil science, with a focus on quantitative pedology. His work aims to improve our understanding of multidimensional soil resilience and soil multifunctionality, and to advance soil knowledge and decision-support systems in resource-poor regions.
He has lived and worked across Southern, Centeral and Eastern Africa, from national-scale soil mapping to extension work with smallholder farmers on heavily leached soil.
His research has been funded through the South African National Research Foundation, The Southern African Science Service Centre for Climate Change and Adaptive Land Management (SASSCAL), EU Horizon 2020, EU LIFE and the Australian Research Council, and he has assembled international consortia for World Bank and BRICS proposals. He has taught crop and soil science at university level and introduced a course in digital soil mapping and remote sensing in agriculture at Stellenbosch University.
He publishes with a global network of collaborators in journals including Geoderma, Science of the Total Environment, Catena, Pedosphere, and Journal of Environmental Management.
